name: Timex Group India Ltd
tagline: High-quality, cash-backed 40%+ growth from an e-commerce channel-mix shift -- but the promoter (Baupost's Timex Group Luxury Watches BV) has cut its stake from ~75% to 51% in a year, growth is decelerating, and the stock trades at ~74x earnings after a 106% run
business_overview: Timex Group India (TGIL) designs, markets, sells, and services Timex-branded watches in India, and also distributes Guess and Versace watches, having taken over full brand ownership from its former Titan partnership in 2013.
fundamentals_table: Rs 419 Cr / Rs 538 Cr / Rs 799 Cr (+48% FY26)
Rs 21 Cr / Rs 31 Cr / Rs 75 Cr (PBT +138% FY26)
Revenue Rs 219 Cr (+30% YoY), EBITDA Rs 35.8 Cr (16.3% margin, +63% YoY), PBT Rs 33.8 Cr (+70%), PAT Rs 25 Cr (+70.5%)
E-commerce +67%, Trade +51%; e-commerce ~40% of revenue (from ~5% four years ago)
~74.93% (Mar 2025) -> 59.93% (Jun 2025 OFS at Rs 175) -> 51.00% (Dec 2025 OFS at Rs 275); parent says no further sales
Borrowings Rs 71 Cr (down from Rs 86 Cr); FY26 CFO Rs 91 Cr, FCF Rs 89 Cr (~ PAT), CFO/OP 104%
fundamentals_narrative: The growth is real and unusually high-quality: FY26 revenue Rs 799 Cr (+48%), PBT +138%, EBITDA margin stepped from ~13% to 16.3% in Q1 FY27, and cash conversion is excellent (FY26 CFO Rs 91 Cr, FCF Rs 89 Cr roughly equal to PAT, CFO/operating-profit 104%). The structural driver -- e-commerce scaling from ~5% to ~40% of revenue in four years, still +67% YoY in Q1 FY27, with quick-commerce dark stores ramping -- is genuine and continuing. The deep read, however, enlarges the promoter-selling concern the earlier pass treated as minor: Timex Group Luxury Watches BV (ultimately Baupost Group) cut its holding from ~74.93% in March 2025 to 51.00% by June 2026 through two offers for sale -- a 15% tranche in June 2025 at a Rs 175 floor and a further ~9% in December 2025 at a Rs 275 floor -- versus the current Rs 654 price. The parent has since publicly ruled out further sales and reaffirmed control at 51%. Alongside this, Q1 FY27 revenue growth decelerated to +30% from FY26's +48%. At ~74x trailing earnings and ~87x book after a 106% one-year run, the valuation prices in sustained 40%+ compounding that the latest quarter no longer shows.
sentiment_summary: Read the entire 32-post thread (all of it fits in one batch). Thread is thin (32 posts since Dec 2022) but every recent post confirms strong, ongoing execution; most recent post is from 3 days before this scan (Aug 20, 2026).
community_signal: Satishwe (trusted, elevated-tier) posted detailed AGM/results notes twice (Aug 2025 and Aug 2026), most recently the 38th AGM highlights: 48% FY26 growth split half value/half volume, e-commerce now 40% of revenue (up from 5% four years ago, growing 90% YoY), trade channel 33% (+32%), OEM 15% (+43%). GurpreetSingh (Feb 2026) confirmed Q3 FY26 revenue +26% YoY, EBITDA +122% YoY, 9M revenue +40%, with Timex-branded products the fastest-growing at +52%. saranshbagdi (Jan 2026) flagged the promoter selling ~9% of holding (down to ~51%) since the 2020 Baupost Group acquisition of the global parent -- a monetization event to watch but not disqualifying given majority control is retained.
bull_case: High-quality earnings: FY26 FCF Rs 89 Cr roughly equals PAT, CFO/operating-profit 104%, working capital cut to 49 days from 63 -- growth is genuinely cash-backed, not accrual
Real structural driver: e-commerce scaled from ~5% to ~40% of revenue in four years and still grew 67% YoY in Q1 FY27; quick-commerce dark-store expansion adds a further leg
Operating leverage on an asset-light licensee model: EBITDA margin rose to 16.3% in Q1 FY27 from ~13%, PBT +70% on revenue +30%
Low, reducing debt (borrowings Rs 71 Cr from Rs 86 Cr); trade channel still growing 51% on higher per-door productivity
Promoter parent has now publicly ruled out further stake sales and reaffirmed its 51% controlling position
bear_case: Promoter sell-down is large, not minor: Timex Group Luxury Watches BV (Baupost) cut its stake from ~74.93% to 51.00% via two OFS in 2025 at Rs 175 and Rs 275 floors -- roughly a third of the promoter holding, sold well below the current Rs 654 price
Growth is decelerating: Q1 FY27 revenue +30% YoY versus FY26's +48% -- at a ~74x multiple, any sustained slowdown re-rates the stock hard
Extreme valuation: ~74x trailing P/E, ~87x book, ~45-50x EV/EBITDA after a 106% one-year run -- the price already assumes years of 40%+ compounding
No equity dividend despite consistent profitability and strong FCF -- capital-return signal is weak while the promoter is a financial sponsor monetising its position
Very high ROE/ROCE figures largely reflect a tiny equity base, not a defensible moat; the watch category is competitive (Titan dominates, smartwatch players crowd the low end)
Thin forum coverage (~32 posts) means limited independent scrutiny
verdict_headline: Genuinely high-quality, cash-backed growth on a real e-commerce channel shift -- but a large promoter sell-down, decelerating growth and a ~74x multiple cap the forward return
verdict_reasoning: Earnings quality is a genuine positive: FCF roughly equals PAT, cash conversion is 104%, and the e-commerce mix shift (5% -> 40% of revenue) is a real structural driver still growing 67% YoY

But the deep read materially enlarges the promoter concern: the Baupost-controlled parent reduced its holding from ~75% to 51% through two 2025 OFS at Rs 175 and Rs 275 -- far below today's Rs 654 -- which, together with Q1 FY27 growth decelerating to +30% from FY26's +48%, is a poor setup at a ~74x P/E / ~87x P/B valuation

No red flag and control is retained at 51% with a stated end to sales, so this is not a HIGH CAUTION case -- but thesis-fit moves to 'neither' (a 10x from ~Rs 6,600 Cr at this multiple is not a realistic base case) and conviction eases from Medium-High to Medium

deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium-High -> Medium. Growth is real and unusually high-quality (FY26 revenue +48%, FCF ~ PAT, CFO/OP 104%, EBITDA margin 13% -> 16.3%, e-commerce 5% -> 40% of revenue). But the deep read enlarges the promoter-selling concern the prior pass under-weighted -- Timex Group Luxury Watches BV (Baupost) cut its stake from ~75% to 51% via two 2025 OFS at Rs 175 and Rs 275 vs Rs 654 now -- and Q1 FY27 revenue growth decelerated to +30% from FY26's +48%. At ~74x trailing P/E / ~87x P/B after a 106% one-year run, thesis-fit drops to 'neither' and conviction to Medium. Control retained at 51% with a stated end to sales, so not a HIGH CAUTION case.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~74x trailing P/E on a branded-consumer name implies the market is pricing 40%+ sustained EPS CAGR for several years against, say, a ~38x exit -- essentially a continuation of the FY26 pace, not the +30% Q1 FY27 delivered

market_expectation.gap_basis: the ~74x multiple prices a longer runway of 40%+ growth than the latest print supports; with Q1 FY27 at +30% and a known promoter seller at 51%, our FY28 PAT path is likely a touch below what the multiple implies rather than above it
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

catalyst.event: H2 FY27 prints showing whether revenue growth re-accelerates toward 40% or settles near 30%, plus confirmation the promoter sell-down is genuinely over (no further OFS / block deal)

value_chain.theme: digital-first, premiumising discretionary consumption in India (branded watches / fashion accessories)
value_chain.position: brand licensee and distributor -- Timex India rights plus Guess & Versace distribution; asset-light design / marketing / omnichannel distribution, limited assembly
value_chain.bottleneck_node: brand equity + omnichannel distribution reach (D2C / e-commerce / quick-commerce); value is captured in channel mix, not manufacturing
value_chain.note: Not a capacity-cycle story. The driver is a channel-mix shift -- e-commerce ~5% -> ~40% of revenue in four years, quick-commerce ramping, trade-door productivity up -- in a category where Titan dominates the mass segment and smartwatch players crowd the low end, so Timex's edge is a niche brand plus omnichannel execution rather than a structural moat.

drivers: operating leverage on an asset-light licensee model (structural)
earnings_quality.normalised_note: EBITDA margin has stepped from ~13% to ~16% on mix and operating leverage with no obvious cyclical or one-off inflator, and FCF roughly equals PAT. Quarterly margin is seasonal (Dec-2024 quarter fell to 6% OPM), so a single strong quarter should not be annualised, but the through-cycle trend is genuinely upward.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: YoY revenue growth: FY25 +28%; FY26 ran hot (9M FY26 +40%, Q3 FY26 EBITDA +122%), FY26 full year +48%; Q1 FY27 +30% -- a clear step down in the growth rate. E-commerce still +67% YoY in Q1 FY27 but off a now-larger ~40% revenue share.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: At ~74x trailing P/E the multiple needs 40%+ sustained EPS CAGR against a ~38x exit; Q1 FY27's +30% revenue growth is already below that pace, so the price is set for a re-acceleration or a longer runway than the latest print supports -- the de-rating risk if growth settles near 30%.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Asset-light, low debt (borrowings Rs 71 Cr from Rs 86 Cr), FY26 FCF Rs 89 Cr ~ PAT, working capital cut to 49 days from 63 -- operationally disciplined. But no equity dividend despite consistent profitability and strong FCF, and the promoter (Timex Group Luxury Watches BV / Baupost) sold ~24pp of its stake via two OFS in 2025 (at Rs 175 and Rs 275) taking holding from ~75% to 51%.
